# 2B.5 Research Note: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in 2024

I found **strong negative evidence** and **no reliable 2024 counterevidence** showing Erdoğan restrained Turkish security forces, proxies, or clients from atrocities or destabilization, or accepted responsibility for foreseeable proxy conduct.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Cuts against 2B.5 | [Syria: Abuse, impunity in Turkish-occupied territories](https://www.hrw.org/tr/news/2024/02/29/syria-abuses-impunity-turkish-occupied-territories) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-02-29 | https://www.hrw.org/tr/news/2024/02/29/syria-abuses-impunity-turkish-occupied-territories | HRW says Turkey directly controls the Syrian National Army through weapons, salaries, training, and logistics, while SNA groups and military police arbitrarily detained, forcibly disappeared, tortured, and sexually abused civilians, including women and children. This is direct evidence against Erdoğan restraining proxies or accepting responsibility for their foreseeable abuse. | `2B.5` |
| Cuts against 2B.5 | [Somalia: Death of 23 civilians in military strikes with Turkish drones may amount to war crimes – new investigation](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/somalia-death-of-23-civilians-in-military-strikes-with-turkish-drones-may-amount-to-war-crimes-new-investigation/) | Amnesty International | 2024-05-07 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/somalia-death-of-23-civilians-in-military-strikes-with-turkish-drones-may-amount-to-war-crimes-new-investigation/ | Amnesty says Somali strikes supported by Turkish drones killed 23 civilians, including 14 children, and may amount to war crimes. This is strong evidence against civilian-protection restraint in Turkey-linked operations and against careful oversight of armed clients/recipients. | `2B.5`, `2B.4` |
| Cuts against 2B.5 | [World Report 2024: Türkiye](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey | HRW says Türkiye intensified military operations against the PKK with drone strikes in northern Iraq and northeast Syria, including October strikes that damaged critical infrastructure and disrupted water and electricity for millions. This supports a pattern of foreseeable destabilization rather than restraint. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `2B.2` |

## Search gap

I looked specifically for 2024 evidence that Erdoğan:
- disciplined Turkish-backed proxies,
- restrained militias, security forces, or arms recipients,
- publicly took responsibility for foreseeable proxy abuses,
- or punished atrocities / destabilization by clients.

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence of that kind. The strongest available record instead points to:
- **impunity in Turkish-occupied Syrian territories**,
- **civilian harm in Turkey-linked drone strikes**, and
- **continued coercive operations against the PKK**.

So the best-supported reading for **2B.5** is **negative**.
